jp: 事故[じこ]{の|no-possessive}こと{など|nado-etc}想像[そうぞう]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}したくない。
en: I don't even want to imagine something like an accident.
why: だに attaches to the verb noun 想像 and means 'not even (to imagine)'; the others do not give that sense.

jp: 彼[かれ]{が|ga-subject}会社[かいしゃ]{を|o-object}辞[や]める{なんて|nanka-nante}、誰[だれ]{も|mo-total-negation}想像[そうぞう]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}しなかった。
en: No one even imagined that he would quit the company.
why: 想像だにしない is a fixed pattern meaning 'did not even imagine'.

jp: 戦争[せんそう]{の|no-possessive}悲惨[ひさん]さ{は|wa-topic}、想像[そうぞう]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}できない。
en: The misery of war is beyond even imagining.
why: だに marks the minimal act, imagining, as impossible too: 'cannot even imagine'.

jp: 兵士[へいし]{は|wa-topic}微動[びどう]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}せず、門[もん]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に/で|ni-location}立[た]っていた。
en: The soldier stood in front of the gate without moving a muscle.
why: 微動だにしない is a set phrase: not even the slightest movement.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]{は|wa-topic}私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}忠告[ちゅうこく]{を|o-object}一顧[いっこ]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}しなかった。
en: She did not give my advice so much as a glance.
why: 一顧だにしない is a set phrase: did not even spare a glance, ignored completely.

jp: あの日[ひ]{の|no-possessive}こと{は|wa-topic}、考[かんが]える{だに|dani}恐[おそ]ろしい。
en: Even to think of that day is frightening.
why: After a dictionary-form verb, だに means 'merely to (think of it)'; すら and さえ cannot follow a bare verb.

jp: あの夜[よる]{の|no-possessive}出来事[できごと]{は|wa-topic}、思[おも]い出[だ]す{だに|dani}身震[みぶる]い{が|ga-sense}する。
en: Even recalling the events of that night makes me shudder.
why: Verb + だに means 'merely to (recall it)', followed by a strong reaction.

jp: 彼[かれ]{の|no-possessive}不幸[ふこう]{を|o-object}聞[き]く{だに|dani}胸[むね]{が|ga-subject}痛[いた]む。
en: My heart aches even to hear of his misfortune.
why: 聞くだに is a fixed literary pattern: 'merely to hear (it)'.

jp: 観客[かんきゃく]{は|wa-topic}身[み]じろぎ{だに/すら/さえ|dani}せず、演奏[えんそう]{に|ni-target}聞[き]き入[い]っていた。
en: The audience listened to the performance, rapt, without so much as stirring.
why: 身じろぎだにせず is a set phrase: without making even the slightest movement.

jp: 優勝[ゆうしょう]{など|nado-etc}、予想[よそう]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}できなかった。
en: We couldn't even have predicted winning.
why: 予想だにできない means 'could not even foresee'; だに names the most basic act as impossible.

jp: 彼[かれ]{の|no-possessive}名前[なまえ]{は|wa-topic}、口[くち]{に|ni-change}する{だに|dani}汚[けが]らわしい。
en: His name is vile even to utter.
why: Verb + だに means 'merely to say it', followed by a strong judgement.

jp: 被災地[ひさいち]{の|no-possessive}惨状[さんじょう]{は|wa-topic}、写真[しゃしん]{で|de-means}見[み]る{だに|dani}痛[いた]ましい。
en: The devastation in the disaster area is painful even to see in photographs.
why: Verb + だに means 'merely to look at it', then a strong feeling follows.

jp: もしあの時[とき]遅[おく]れていたら{と|to-quote}思[おも]う{だに|dani}ぞっとする。
en: I shudder even to think what would have happened if I had been late then.
why: 思うだに means 'merely to think (of it)', then a shudder follows.

jp: 道端[みちばた]{の|no-possessive}募金箱[ぼきんばこ]{を|o-object}一瞥[いちべつ]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}せず、彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}通[とお]り過[す]ぎた。
en: He walked past the donation box by the road without even a glance.
why: 一瞥だにせず means 'without even a glance'; だに names the smallest possible act.

jp: 最初[さいしょ]{から|kara-from}、成功[せいこう]{など|nado-etc}期待[きたい]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}していなかった。
en: From the start, I hadn't even hoped for success.
why: 期待だにしない means 'not even hope for it', denying the most basic act.

jp: 村[むら]{に|ni-location}人影[ひとかげ]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}なかった。
en: There was not even a trace of a person in the village.
why: 人影だになかった means 'not even a shadow of a person', the minimum, was there.

jp: 親[おや]{が|ga-subject}子[こ]{を|o-object}失[うしな]う悲[かな]しみ{は|wa-topic}、想像[そうぞう]する{だに|dani}耐[た]えがたい。
en: The grief of a parent losing a child is unbearable even to imagine.
why: Verb + だに means 'merely to imagine it', then an extreme judgement follows.

jp: どんなに風[かぜ]{が|ga-subject}吹[ふ]い{ても|te-mo}、その大木[たいぼく]{は|wa-topic}微動[びどう]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}しなかった。
en: However hard the wind blew, that big tree did not stir in the least.
why: 微動だにしなかった means 'did not move even slightly'.

jp: 遺族[いぞく]{の|no-possessive}気持[きも]ち{を|o-object}思[おも]う{だに|dani}、涙[なみだ]{が|ga-subject}出[で]る。
en: Merely thinking of how the bereaved family feels brings tears to my eyes.
why: Verb + だに means 'merely to think of it', followed by a strong reaction.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]{は|wa-topic}別[わか]れ{の|no-possessive}時[とき]、一言[ひとこと]{だに/すら/さえ|dani}話[はな]さなかった。
en: At the farewell, she did not say a single word.
why: 一言だに話さなかった means 'did not even say one word', the smallest possible amount.
